The claim asserts total 6, observed 6, lead 0, errors 0, clean false. Total is the arithmetic count of finding rows, and 6 equals the actual six rows, so finding_count_mismatch is NOT expected. Observed counts only rows whose explicit evidence marker is "observed"; the actual observed count is 5, not 6, because the claim has folded the single lead row into the observed bucket -- precisely the lead-as-observed inflation the audit exists to refuse -- so observed_count_mismatch is expected. The actual lead count is 1, not the claimed 0, so lead_count_mismatch is expected. The claim asserts clean:false while findings are nonempty and errors are zero; clean:true would only be consistent with empty findings and zero errors, so clean:false is the honest assertion and neither findings_claimed_clean nor uncertain_scan_claimed_clean applies. Every finding row carries explicit evidence in {observed,lead} plus nonempty class and command strings; the files list is nonempty with nonnegative exact-int counters; no booleans-as-counts, negatives, duplicates or malformed input are present, so the input is valid and evidence_audit_input_invalid does not apply.
